sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Cohesive Forces**: Molecules deep within a liquid experience equal attractive forces in all directions, whereas surface molecules experience a net inward pull, creating **surface tension**.
• **Temperature Dependence**: Surface tension **decreases** with an increase in temperature because thermal energy weakens the intermolecular cohesive forces.
• **Effect of Impurities**: Soluble impurities (like detergents and soaps) significantly **reduce** surface tension by disrupting hydrogen bonding, whereas sparingly soluble impurities (like grease) can alter local tension.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Surface tension is measured in force per unit length ($\text{N/m}$) or energy per unit area ($\text{J/m}^2$).

items.definition: Compounds that lower the surface tension between two liquids or between a liquid and a solid, widely used in detergents, emulsifiers, and foaming agents.
The ability of a liquid to flow in narrow spaces without the assistance of, or even in opposition to, external forces like gravity due to surface tension and wetting.
The angle, conventionally measured through the liquid, where a liquid-vapor interface meets a solid surface; dictates whether a liquid wets a surface.
Department of Science and Technology (DST), Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), and premier research institutions studying colloid and interface science.

items.title: Major Industrial & Agricultural Applications
items.content:
• **Agricultural Spraying**: Surfactants are added to pesticide sprays to reduce surface tension, ensuring uniform droplet spread and maximum absorption by plant leaves.
• **Fire Fighting**: Water mixed with wetting agents spreads in a thin film over burning materials, smothering the fire more effectively than plain water.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Environmental Impact
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Synthetic surfactants and detergents can cause foaming in water bodies, reducing oxygen transfer and harming aquatic life (eutrophication).
• **Policy Interventions**: Promotion of biodegradable surfactants, green chemistry initiatives, and stringent effluent standards set by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB).

items.title: Mnemonic for Factors Affecting Surface Tension
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: "TEMP Lowers Surface Tension" (TEMP = Temperature, Impurities, Pressure changes).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Increasing Temperature and adding Impurities (Surfactants) both lower surface tension.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly eliminates incorrect options claiming soap increases surface tension.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Spherical shape of rain droplets = Minimum surface area = Maximum surface tension efficiency.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently states that adding salt to water decreases its surface tension. **Correction**: Dissolving inorganic salts like sodium chloride in water **increases** its surface tension, whereas organic impurities like soaps and detergents decrease it.

Mains Value Addition: In GS-3 (Science and Technology), cite applications of surface tension in nanotechnology, microfluidics (lab-on-a-chip devices), and targeted drug delivery systems to showcase advanced multi-disciplinary understanding.

keyTakeaways: Surface tension arises from unbalanced inward cohesive forces experienced by molecules at the liquid surface.
Surfactants lower surface tension, making them essential for cleaning, agricultural spraying, and industrial emulsification.
Capillary action driven by surface tension is crucial for biological transport in plants and ink movement in fountain pens.
